turns.doctor_question: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you into the clinic today?
turns.patient_response:
Well, my job actually sent me here. I do general maintenance and repair, and lately, I just... I keep forgetting my scheduled callbacks and work orders. Like, just the other day I was supposed to fix this leaky P-trap under a sink in one of the main offices. It's one of those old PVC ones, and honestly, the contractors who installed them back in the day did a terrible job, they didn't even use the right sealant. I was telling my brother about it—he used to do construction before he hurt his back, now he just does dispatch, but he knows all about those shoddy pipe jobs. 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, the clinic. Yeah, so I completely forgot to actually go back and finish that sink. And it's not just that, I keep forgetting basic follow-ups I promised people all over the building, and the paperwork has just piled up so much. It got to the point where my boss pulled me aside and basically told me I had to come here and get this sorted out, because I'm up for a senior spot and he said I'm gonna lose my shot at moving up if I keep dropping the ball. So... yeah, that's why I'm sitting here.

symptom_reasoning.S004: The patient describes failing to finish workplace duties, such as not completing the repair on a sink and letting paperwork pile up.
symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient gets distracted by unrelated thoughts about plumbing contractors and their brother, causing them to lose their train of thought mid-sentence.
symptom_reasoning.S009: The patient explicitly states they keep forgetting scheduled callbacks, work orders, and basic follow-ups in their daily work activities.

turns.doctor_question: Have you struggled with keeping track of things like this since you were a kid, or is this a brand-new issue for you?
turns.patient_response: Oh, no, it's definitely not new. I remember being exactly like this way back in grade school, honestly. Long before any of this pressure at work. My teachers always told my parents I was bright, but I was constantly misplacing my homework or losing important permission slips. It was a whole thing. Like, I remember this one time in fourth grade, Mrs. Gable's class—she had this huge collection of ceramic frogs on her desk, which I always thought was so weird. Who collects frogs? Anyway, she would always have to tap my desk because I'd miss half the directions for our assignments. I'd be looking at the frogs or staring out the window at the playground, and then everyone else would be working, and I'd have no idea what we were supposed to be doing. I always needed her to come over and remind me to actually finish my classwork. My mom tried buying me all those color-coded folders to help me keep track of papers, the Lisa Frank ones, you know? With the neon leopards and stuff. I loved those folders, but I'd still just shove everything into my backpack loose anyway... so, yeah, I guess I've always kind of been this way.

symptom_reasoning.S003: The patient describes the teacher having to tap her desk because she wasn't listening and missed directions.
symptom_reasoning.S004: The patient states she always needed reminders to actually finish her classwork.
symptom_reasoning.S005: The patient describes struggling to organize her papers, shoving them loosely into her backpack instead of using folders.
symptom_reasoning.S007: The patient reports constantly misplacing homework and losing important permission slips.
symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient describes being easily distracted by extraneous stimuli, such as ceramic frogs on the teacher's desk or looking out the window.

turns.doctor_question: Do you often feel physically restless or like you constantly need to be moving around, as if driven by a motor?
turns.patient_response:
No, not really. I mean, I'm pretty tired most of the time, honestly. My job keeps me on my feet all day, walking back and forth across the facility, up and down ladders. Like, yesterday I had to replace the ballast in these fluorescent lights in the main hallway. Have you ever noticed how those lights hum? It drives me absolutely crazy. I tried telling the facility manager we should just switch everything to LED, it saves money on the electric bill and they don't make that awful buzzing noise. My neighbor, Dave, he just redid his whole garage with LEDs and it looks amazing. He’s got this vintage Mustang he’s restoring, beautiful car, cherry red. He spends every weekend out there just tinkering with the engine. I helped him bleed the brakes a few weeks ago... 

But anyway, what were you asking? Oh, right, restless. No, I don't really feel like I need to be moving all the time. If anything, when I get home, I just want to sit on the couch and not move a muscle.

symptom_reasoning.S008: The patient demonstrates distractibility by unrelated thoughts during the response, drifting from their job to fluorescent lights, LEDs, their neighbor's garage, and a vintage car before remembering the original question.
symptom_reasoning.S012: The patient explicitly denies feeling physically restless, stating they do not feel the need to be moving all the time.
symptom_reasoning.S014: The patient denies feeling driven by a motor or needing to constantly move, noting they just want to sit on the couch and not move a muscle after work.
